"""OdinExerciseGenerationConsumer — drains ``range.odin_exercise.generate.>``
(ticket #1724, Task 7).

The orchestrating worker for the ODIN-grounded exercise-generation ladder:
one JetStream message drives all FOUR steps of
``fetch_odin -> generate_factions -> analyze_environment -> finalize_scenario``,
persisting a cursor (``range.odin_generation_run.step`` / ``step_status`` /
``steps_done``) after each so a NAK'd redelivery (rate-limit backoff) resumes
at the right step instead of restarting the whole run and re-spending its
already-completed LLM calls.

This is genuinely new code, not a subclass of either single-shot generator
it reuses — ~85% of a single-shot consumer (claim/coalesce, cancel
checkpoints, rate-limit, persistence, audit, fan-out, settle, progress,
ack/nak) is hard-coded to that generator's own row semantics. What IS reused
is narrow and explicit:

  - ``run_faction_discovery`` / ``run_environment_analysis``
    (``workers/generation/{faction_discovery,environment_analysis}/
    generate.py``, Task 4) — the pure "build messages -> call the LLM ->
    validate" cores, with classification staying at THIS call site.
  - ``resolve_odin_grounding`` / ``load_odin_oe_for_grounding``
    (``workers/generation/odin_exercise/grounding.py``, Task 6) — step 1's
    entire implementation.
  - ``handlers.analysis._factions_list`` — the EXISTING candidates -> PMESII
    payload projector (step 3 builds throwaway ``AnalysisFaction`` proto
    messages from the discovery candidates purely so this shared projector,
    not a second hand-rolled one, produces the ``factions`` payload key).
  - ``faction_discovery_upsert_pending`` / ``analysis_upsert_pending`` (the
    SAME functions + the SAME ``pg_advisory_xact_lock`` keys the
    DiscoverFactions / AnalyzeEnvironment RPC handlers use) — so a
    concurrent user-initiated manual Suggest/Analyze on the SAME wizard
    draft coalesces onto (or is coalesced by) this run exactly as it would
    coalesce with another manual request today.

Ladder mechanics, per ``_compute``:

    1. Read the run by its wizard draft handle (``faction_discovery_draft_id``
       — the payload's OWN identity key, not a bare ``run_id`` lookup, since
       no such lookup exists; the run table's uniqueness IS this draft id).
       Unclaimable (row gone / a stale job_id from a superseded request /
       already terminal) -> settle the job row + an error frame + ACK, no
       processing. Mirrors ``FactionDiscoveryConsumer._compute``'s own
       claim-returned-None branch (:341-366) and its documented tradeoff: a
       lost-ACK redelivery of an already-SUCCEEDED run also lands here and
       is reported as 'error' — the ``generation_job_settle`` CAS is what
       keeps that cosmetic (it can never downgrade an actually-completed
       job's row).
    2. Cancel checkpoint (before any wall-clock or LLM spend).
    3. Re-stamp ``deadline_at = now() + RANGE_ODIN_GEN_DEADLINE_S`` — this
       happens on EVERY successful claim, including a NAK'd resume, so a
       long rate-limit backoff does not eat into the SAME fixed budget the
       first attempt already spent; the sweep loop below is the real
       backstop against a truly abandoned (crashed-worker) row.
    4. Loop the four steps in ``_STEP_ORDER``, skipping any ``idx <
       run.steps_done`` (the resume path — deliberately NOT user-facing:
       no frame is emitted for a skipped step). Per remaining step: re-check
       cancel; compute ``budget = min(step_budget_s, deadline_at - now())``
       and fail the run with ``error_code='timeout'`` WITHOUT an LLM call
       when that is <= 0; claim the step (bumps ``step_attempts``, flips the
       row to 'computing'); extend the JetStream ack; emit the entry frame;
       run the step under ``asyncio.wait_for(..., budget)``; classify any
       exception per Task 4's taxonomy; on success, mark the step ``done``
       (each step method does this itself, in the SAME tx as its own domain
       write) and emit the exit frame.
    5. Step 4 (``finalize_scenario``) makes NO LLM call and does not go
       through the generic post-step "mark done + emit exit frame" tail —
       it settles the WHOLE RUN's terminal state (assemble ``scenario`` +
       ``status='ready'`` + audit + outbox in one tx, THEN
       ``generation_job_settle`` (before the terminal frame, mirroring
       ``FactionDiscoveryConsumer``'s own ordering), THEN the
       ``status="ready"`` frame) inside its own step method.

Rate limiting (2 of 4 steps, never 1 or 4): one ``self.rate_limiter.
consume()`` call immediately before EACH of ``run_faction_discovery`` and
``run_environment_analysis``, using a SECOND, dedicated ``RateLimiter``
instance (``RANGE_ODIN_GEN_RATE_CAPACITY``/``_REFILL_PER_MINUTE``, default
20/20 — see ``worker.py``'s construction site) — never the shared 60/60
instance every other generator shares, and never keyed on the bare
``org_id`` (see :data:`_ODIN_GEN_BUCKET_NS`'s docstring for why that would
silently collide with the shared instance's bucket row). On exhaustion this
adopts faction's own recovery behaviour: the run resets ``computing ->
pending`` (preserving which step it was on), the step's own ``step_status``
resets to ``pending`` too, and the message NAKs with the server-advised
delay — but only AFTER a frame carrying ``retry_after_ms`` ships, so a long
backoff is not unexplained silence on the wire.

Cancellation and timeout are BOTH ``status='error'`` on the row (never a
fifth status — the TS ``ResumableRow`` parser is pinned to exactly the four
migration 00095 defines), discriminated only by ``error_code`` (
``cancelled`` / ``timeout``). The terminal WIRE frame is free to use a
richer vocabulary (``job_progress.go`` closes the SSE stream on any of
``completed|failed|ready|error|cancelled``), so a cancel's frame says
``status="cancelled"`` while its ROW says ``status='error'``.

Gate 3 / RLS: every domain write runs under ``pool.with_org(org_id)``.
BYPASSRLS (``pool.with_drain()``) is used ONLY for two cross-tenant reads
that must run before an org context exists: the run lookup in ``_on_poison``
and the deadline sweep's discovery pass (:func:`odin_generation_sweep_
expired` in ``repo/queries/odin_generation_run.py``). The ODIN cache tables
(read by step 1, via ``grounding.load_odin_oe_for_grounding``) are read on
the APP ROLE via ``pool.app.acquire()`` — NEVER ``with_drain()`` (the
drainer role has no grants on those tables at all; they carry no org_id/RLS
by design).

Gate 6: the only direct (non-outbox) publish here is job progress —
everything else (the step-4 terminal write, its audit twin, and its
``range.feed.updated.<requested_by>`` fan-out) goes through the outbox
inside the SAME tx as the domain write.

This module also owns the deadline sweep (:func:`sweep_expired_odin_
generation_runs` / :func:`odin_generation_deadline_sweep_loop`) — the
worker-crash backstop for a run stranded in 'computing' with no redelivery
ever arriving to resume it. Registered on the SAME hourly cadence as the
other periodic sweeps (``consumer_base.ORPHAN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S``), in
``worker.py``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any, ClassVar, Final

import structlog
from omnicore.range.analysis.v1 import analysis_pb2

from range_svc.audit.emit import ActiveKeyProvider, emit_audit
from range_svc.handlers.analysis import _factions_list
from range_svc.llm import LLMRateLimited
from range_svc.repo import queries as q
from range_svc.workers.consumer_base import (
    ORPHAN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S as ORPHAN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S,  # re-export (worker.py + wrapper default)
)
from range_svc.workers.consumer_base import (
    PullConsumer,
    diagnosable_error,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.environment_analysis.generate import (
    run_environment_analysis,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.environment_analysis.validator import (
    AnalysisValidationError,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.faction_discovery.consumer import (
    _DEFAULT_COUNT,
    CAUSE_TIMEOUT,
    classify_llm_failure,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.faction_discovery.generate import (
    render_location,
    render_objective,
    run_faction_discovery,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.faction_discovery.validator import (
    DiscoveryValidationError,
)
from range_svc.workers.generation.odin_exercise.grounding import (
    OdinGrounding,
    OdinLocation,
    OdinObjective,
    load_odin_oe_for_grounding,
    resolve_odin_grounding,
)
from range_svc.workers.progress import emit_progress

_log = structlog.stdlib.get_logger("range_svc.workers.generation.odin_exercise")

_SERVICE_ACCOUNT = "range-svc-worker"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ladder shape

_STEP_FETCH_ODIN: Final[str] = "fetch_odin"
_STEP_GENERATE_FACTIONS: Final[str] = "generate_factions"
_STEP_ANALYZE_ENVIRONMENT: Final[str] = "analyze_environment"
_STEP_FINALIZE_SCENARIO: Final[str] = "finalize_scenario"

#: Persisted step ids, in ladder order (migration 00095's exact vocabulary —
#: never reorder without also reordering the budgets below).
_STEP_ORDER: Final[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = (
    _STEP_FETCH_ODIN,
    _STEP_GENERATE_FACTIONS,
    _STEP_ANALYZE_ENVIRONMENT,
    _STEP_FINALIZE_SCENARIO,
)
_STEP_INDEX: Final[dict[str, int]] = {step: idx for idx, step in enumerate(_STEP_ORDER)}
_TOTAL_STEPS: Final[int] = len(_STEP_ORDER)

#: Per-step wall-clock budget (seconds). ``fetch_odin`` is a stuck-pool
#: detector (pure DB read, no LLM); ``generate_factions``/``analyze_
#: environment`` each wrap one LLM call whose own read timeout is 20s (45s
#: makes a hung gateway surface as a STEP timeout, not a silent hang);
#: ``finalize_scenario`` makes no LLM call at all.
_STEP_BUDGETS_S: Final[dict[str, float]] = {
    _STEP_FETCH_ODIN: 10.0,
    _STEP_GENERATE_FACTIONS: 45.0,
    _STEP_ANALYZE_ENVIRONMENT: 45.0,
    _STEP_FINALIZE_SCENARIO: 10.0,
}

#: Default whole-run deadline (seconds) — overridden by
#: ``Config.range_odin_gen_deadline_s`` (``RANGE_ODIN_GEN_DEADLINE_S``) at
#: construction time in ``worker.py``. MUST stay below ``ack_wait_s`` (see
#: the ``OdinExerciseGenerationConsumer`` docstring) — a run must terminate
#: itself before JetStream would redeliver it out from under a live attempt.
_DEFAULT_DEADLINE_S: Final[float] = 240.0

#: Fixed namespace for this generator's rate-limit bucket key. ``range.
#: consume_ai_rate_token`` keys its token-bucket row on ``bucket_key``
#: ALONE (``org_id`` is stored only for RLS) — passing a BARE ``org_id`` as
#: the bucket key would collide with the shared 60/60 ``RateLimiter``
#: instance every other generator uses (``worker.py``'s ``rate_limiter``),
#: and whichever of the two callers hit the bucket LAST would silently
#: redefine its capacity/refill rate for the other. Namespacing with a
#: fixed, generator-specific UUID5 makes this generator's bucket row
#: structurally distinct from every other org-keyed bucket, at the cost of
#: converting a per-exercise contention domain into an org-wide one — ODIN
#: runs only ever contend with OTHER ODIN runs for the SAME org, never with
#: faction discovery / environment analysis / any other generator.
_ODIN_GEN_BUCKET_NS: Final[uuid.UUID] = uuid.uuid5(
    uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, "odin-exercise-generation.range-svc.omnicore-platform"
)


def _bucket_key(org_id: str) -> str:
    """The namespaced, per-org rate-limit bucket key (see
    :data:`_ODIN_GEN_BUCKET_NS`) — NEVER the bare ``org_id``."""
    return str(uuid.uuid5(_ODIN_GEN_BUCKET_NS, org_id))


class _OdinUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """Step 1: the ODIN cache has no row for the requested template id."""


class _InsufficientOdinContent(RuntimeError):
    """Step 2's defensive empty-context guard tripped (location, objective,
    AND description all blank) — should be effectively unreachable given
    ``resolve_odin_grounding``'s non-empty-description guarantee, but the
    persisted vocabulary carries this error_code specifically for this
    generator, so the guard exists in case that guarantee is ever loosened.
    """


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- step-failure classification


def _classify_step_failure(exc: Exception, *, step_id: str, log: Any) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Classify one step's failure into the persisted ``(error_code,
    error_message)`` pair passed to ``_fail_run``.

    Pure (besides the one diagnostic log line on the generic fallback
    branch) — the ordered ``isinstance`` checks below are the SAME taxonomy,
    in the SAME order, as the ``except`` arms this replaces, producing
    byte-identical strings for every case (the persisted vocabulary these
    strings feed is asserted by tests). ``LLMRateLimited`` is handled by its
    OWN ``except`` arm at the call site, above this one, and never reaches
    here.
    """
    if isinstance(exc, TimeoutError):
        return "timeout", f"step '{step_id}' exceeded its time budget"
    if isinstance(exc, json.JSONDecodeError | DiscoveryValidationError | AnalysisValidationError):
        return "llm_invalid_output", f"invalid AI output: {exc}"
    if isinstance(exc, _OdinUnavailable):
        return "odin_unavailable", str(exc)
    if isinstance(exc, _InsufficientOdinContent):
        return "insufficient_odin_content", str(exc)
    log.error("odin exercise step failed", step=step_id, err=diagnosable_error(exc))
    cause_code, safe_detail = classify_llm_failure(exc)
    error_code = "timeout" if cause_code == CAUSE_TIMEOUT else "llm_failed"
    return error_code, f"[{cause_code}] {safe_detail}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- grounding <-> jsonb


def _grounding_to_jsonb(grounding: OdinGrounding) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize an :class:`OdinGrounding` for the run row's ``grounding``
    JSONB column — persisted so a rate-limit NAK redelivered mid-ladder can
    resume at step 3 without re-deriving step 1's output."""
    return {
        "location": grounding.location.as_dict(),
        "objective": grounding.objective.as_dict(),
        "temporal_context": grounding.temporal_context,
        "description": grounding.description,
        "reference_material": grounding.reference_material,
        "derived_fields": sorted(grounding.derived_fields),
    }


def _grounding_from_jsonb(data: dict[str, Any]) -> OdinGrounding:
    """Inverse of :func:`_grounding_to_jsonb` — reconstructs the
    :class:`OdinGrounding` a resumed run's later steps need, from the
    already-decoded ``run.grounding`` dict."""
    loc = data.get("location") or {}
    obj = data.get("objective") or {}
    return OdinGrounding(
        location=OdinLocation(
            country=str(loc.get("country") or ""),
            town=str(loc.get("town") or ""),
            region=str(loc.get("region") or ""),
        ),
        objective=OdinObjective(
            text=str(obj.get("text") or ""),
            category=str(obj.get("category") or ""),
        ),
        temporal_context=str(data.get("temporal_context") or ""),
        description=str(data.get("description") or ""),
        reference_material=str(data.get("reference_material") or ""),
        derived_fields=frozenset(data.get("derived_fields") or ()),
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- run-row helpers
#
# These three are single-purpose, single-statement raw SQL kept local to this
# module rather than added to repo/queries/odin_generation_run.py: unlike
# odin_generation_sweep_expired (Task 7's one authorized addition to that
# shared module), none of these need to be called from anywhere else, and
# the codebase already keeps this class of one-off statement inline at the
# call site (e.g. the handlers' own ``pg_advisory_xact_lock`` calls).


async def _persist_deadline(conn: Any, *, run_id: str, deadline_at: datetime) -> None:
    """Re-stamp the run's wall-clock deadline at claim time (worker-owned;
    the handler's own ``deadline_at`` at enqueue time is only a placeholder
    until the worker actually claims the run)."""
    await conn.execute(
        "UPDATE range.odin_generation_run SET deadline_at = $2, updated_at = now() WHERE id = $1",
        run_id,
        deadline_at,
    )


async def _reset_run_to_pending(conn: Any, *, run_id: str) -> None:
    """Worker-side recovery: ``computing -> pending``, guarded on
    ``status='computing'`` (a no-op if the crash/backoff predates the claim)
    so a redelivery can re-claim it. Deliberately does NOT touch ``step`` —
    ``claim_step_running`` already stamped it to the step in flight, and
    preserving it is exactly what makes the ladder resume at the RIGHT step
    rather than restarting from ``fetch_odin``. Shared by both the
    rate-limit-exhaustion path and the generic crash-wrapper path (mirrors
    ``faction_discovery_reset_to_pending``'s dual use)."""
    await conn.execute(
        "UPDATE range.odin_generation_run "
        "SET status = 'pending', step_status = 'pending', updated_at = now() "
        "WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'computing'",
        run_id,
    )


async def _settle_cancelled(conn: Any, *, run_id: str) -> None:
    """Worker-side: a cancelled run settles as ``status='error'`` +
    ``error_code='cancelled'`` — NEVER a fifth status (the TS
    ``ResumableRow`` parser is pinned to exactly the four migration 00095
    defines)."""
    await conn.execute(
        "UPDATE range.odin_generation_run "
        "SET status = 'error', "
        "    error_code = 'cancelled', "
        "    error_message = 'cancelled', "
        "    job_id = NULL, "
        "    finished_at = now(), "
        "    updated_at = now() "
        "WHERE id = $1",
        run_id,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- consumer


class OdinExerciseGenerationConsumer(PullConsumer):
    """Pulls ``range.odin_exercise.generate.>`` and drives the 4-step
    ODIN-grounded exercise-generation ladder.

    Constructor args (beyond ``publisher`` from ``PullConsumer``):
        pool:         ``range_svc.db.Pool``
        llm:          ``StubLLM | LiteLLMClient``
        audit_keys:   HMAC key provider
        rate_limiter: a DEDICATED ``RateLimiter`` instance (NOT the shared
                      60/60 instance every other generator uses — see
                      :data:`_ODIN_GEN_BUCKET_NS`'s docstring)
        deadline_s:   the whole-run wall-clock budget (``Config.
                      range_odin_gen_deadline_s`` at the real construction
                      site) — re-stamped on every successful claim.

    ``ack_wait_s`` (300s) MUST exceed ``deadline_s`` (240s default): a run
    is expected to terminate ITSELF (ready/error, including a self-declared
    timeout) well before JetStream would otherwise redeliver the same
    message to a second worker. ``max_deliver=5`` mirrors every other
    generation consumer in this service.

    Does NOT override ``_subscribe`` — the base ``PullConsumer._subscribe``
    already passes ``ack_wait``/``max_deliver`` via ``_ensure_consumer``,
    converging them onto the durable on every subscribe (see
    ``consumer_base.py``'s own module docstring for the landmine overriding
    this re-opens).
    """

    subject_filter: ClassVar[str] = "range.odin_exercise.generate.>"
    durable_name: ClassVar[str] = "range-odin-exercise-generate"
    max_deliver: ClassVar[int] = 5
    ack_wait_s: ClassVar[float] = 300.0

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publisher: Any,
        pool: Any,
        llm: Any,
        audit_keys: ActiveKeyProvider,
        rate_limiter: Any,
        deadline_s: float = _DEFAULT_DEADLINE_S,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(publisher=publisher)
        self.pool = pool
        self.llm = llm
        self.audit_keys = audit_keys
        self.rate_limiter = rate_limiter
        self.deadline_s = deadline_s

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- _handle

    async def _handle(self, msg: Any) -> None:
        """Process one odin_exercise.generate message."""
        log = _log.bind(subject=getattr(msg, "subject", "?"))
        try:
            payload = json.loads(msg.data)
            job_id = str(payload["job_id"] or "")
            run_id = str(payload["run_id"] or "")
            org_id = str(payload.get("org_id", ""))
            requested_by = str(payload["requested_by"] or "")
            faction_draft_id = str(payload["faction_discovery_draft_id"] or "")
            analysis_draft_id = str(payload["analysis_draft_id"] or "")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
            log.error("invalid odin_exercise.generate message payload", err=str(exc))
            await msg.ack()
            return

        # Finding #5 (mirrors FactionDiscoveryConsumer): an empty/missing
        # identity field makes every RLS-scoped write a silent no-op — the
        # RLS policy keys on NULLIF(current_setting(...), '')::uuid, so an
        # empty GUC matches zero rows. Drop the payload (ACK) BEFORE any
        # claim rather than half-processing it.
        if not (
            org_id and job_id and run_id and requested_by and faction_draft_id and analysis_draft_id
        ):
            log.error(
                "odin_exercise.generate payload missing required identity field — dropping",
                has_org_id=bool(org_id),
                has_job_id=bool(job_id),
                has_run_id=bool(run_id),
                has_requested_by=bool(requested_by),
                has_faction_draft_id=bool(faction_draft_id),
                has_analysis_draft_id=bool(analysis_draft_id),
            )
            if job_id:
                await self._publish_job_progress(
                    job_id=job_id,
                    status="error",
                    error="generation request was missing required identity fields",
                    org_id=org_id or None,
                )
            await msg.ack()
            return

        log = log.bind(job_id=job_id, run_id=run_id)

        try:
            await self._compute(
                log,
                payload=payload,
                job_id=job_id,
                run_id=run_id,
                org_id=org_id,
                requested_by=requested_by,
                msg=msg,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            # The claim flips pending->computing; any unexpected error after
            # that would otherwise strand the row in 'computing' forever —
            # reset computing->pending (guarded, a no-op if the crash
            # predates the claim) so redelivery can re-claim + resume at the
            # step it was on, exactly mirroring FactionDiscoveryConsumer's
            # crash-wrapper (:305-322).
            log.error(
                "odin_exercise_generation_compute_dropped — resetting + nacking",
                err=diagnosable_error(exc),
            )
            try:
                async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
                    await _reset_run_to_pending(conn, run_id=run_id)
            except Exception as reset_exc:  # best-effort; nak still fires
                log.warning(
                    "odin_generation_run reset-to-pending failed on crash path",
                    err=str(reset_exc),
                )
            await msg.nak()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- _compute

    async def _compute(
        self,
        log: Any,
        *,
        payload: dict[str, Any],
        job_id: str,
        run_id: str,
        org_id: str,
        requested_by: str,
        msg: Any,
    ) -> None:
        """The 4-step ladder."""
        faction_draft_id = str(payload["faction_discovery_draft_id"])
        analysis_draft_id = str(payload["analysis_draft_id"])
        odin_template_id = str(payload.get("odin_template_id") or "")
        seed = payload.get("seed") or {}
        if not isinstance(seed, dict):
            seed = {}
        faction_count = int(payload.get("faction_count") or 0)

        # Step 1 of the "claim": read the run by its draft handle — the
        # payload's own identity key (there is no bare run_id lookup; the
        # table's sole uniqueness key IS this draft id).
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            run = await q.odin_generation_run_get_by_draft(
                conn, faction_discovery_draft_id=faction_draft_id
            )

        # Unclaimable: the row is gone, belongs to a request superseded by a
        # fresh re-generate (job_id mismatch — the reset upsert always
        # refreshes job_id to the LATEST request's), or already terminal.
        # Mirrors FactionDiscoveryConsumer's claim-returned-None branch
        # (:341-366) including its documented tradeoff: a lost-ACK
        # redelivery of an already-SUCCEEDED run also lands here and is
        # reported 'error' — generation_job_settle's CAS is what keeps that
        # cosmetic (it can never downgrade an actually-completed job).
        if run is None or run.job_id != job_id or run.status not in ("pending", "computing"):
            log.debug("odin generation run not claimable (missing/stale/terminal) — acking")
            async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
                await q.generation_job_settle(conn, job_id=job_id, status="error")
            await self._emit_step_frame(job_id=job_id, org_id=org_id, status="error", generated=0)
            await msg.ack()
            return

        actual_run_id = run.id

        # Cancel checkpoint, before any wall-clock or LLM spend.
        if await self._check_cancelled(org_id=org_id, job_id=job_id):
            await self._cancel(
                org_id=org_id, run_id=actual_run_id, job_id=job_id, generated=run.steps_done
            )
            await msg.ack()
            return

        deadline_at = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(seconds=self.deadline_s)
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await _persist_deadline(conn, run_id=actual_run_id, deadline_at=deadline_at)

        grounding: OdinGrounding | None = (
            _grounding_from_jsonb(run.grounding) if run.grounding else None
        )

        for idx, step_id in enumerate(_STEP_ORDER):
            # Resume path: a step already marked done (persisted
            # steps_done) is never re-run and never re-framed — deliberately
            # not user-facing (this is the rate-limit-NAK resume path).
            if idx < run.steps_done:
                continue

            if await self._check_cancelled(org_id=org_id, job_id=job_id):
                await self._cancel(
                    org_id=org_id, run_id=actual_run_id, job_id=job_id, generated=idx
                )
                await msg.ack()
                return

            remaining_s = (deadline_at - datetime.now(UTC)).total_seconds()
            budget = min(_STEP_BUDGETS_S[step_id], remaining_s)
            if budget <= 0:
                await self._fail_run(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    run_id=actual_run_id,
                    job_id=job_id,
                    step=step_id,
                    step_index=idx,
                    error_code="timeout",
                    error_message="generation run exceeded its overall deadline",
                )
                await msg.ack()
                return

            async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
                await q.odin_generation_run_claim_step_running(
                    conn, run_id=actual_run_id, step=step_id
                )
            await self._extend_ack(msg)
            await self._emit_step_frame(
                job_id=job_id,
                org_id=org_id,
                status="in_progress",
                generated=idx,
                step=step_id,
                step_index=idx,
                step_status="running",
            )

            try:
                if step_id == _STEP_FETCH_ODIN:
                    grounding = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        self._step_fetch_odin(
                            org_id=org_id,
                            run_id=actual_run_id,
                            odin_template_id=odin_template_id,
                            seed=seed,
                        ),
                        timeout=budget,
                    )
                elif step_id == _STEP_GENERATE_FACTIONS:
                    if grounding is None:
                        raise _OdinUnavailable("no grounding available for faction discovery")
                    await asyncio.wait_for(
                        self._step_generate_factions(
                            org_id=org_id,
                            run_id=actual_run_id,
                            job_id=job_id,
                            requested_by=requested_by,
                            faction_draft_id=faction_draft_id,
                            grounding=grounding,
                            faction_count=faction_count,
                        ),
                        timeout=budget,
                    )
                elif step_id == _STEP_ANALYZE_ENVIRONMENT:
                    if grounding is None:
                        raise _OdinUnavailable("no grounding available for environment analysis")
                    await asyncio.wait_for(
                        self._step_analyze_environment(
                            org_id=org_id,
                            run_id=actual_run_id,
                            job_id=job_id,
                            requested_by=requested_by,
                            analysis_draft_id=analysis_draft_id,
                            faction_draft_id=faction_draft_id,
                            grounding=grounding,
                            seed=seed,
                        ),
                        timeout=budget,
                    )
                else:
                    if grounding is None:
                        raise _OdinUnavailable("no grounding available for scenario finalization")
                    await asyncio.wait_for(
                        self._step_finalize_scenario(
                            org_id=org_id,
                            run_id=actual_run_id,
                            job_id=job_id,
                            requested_by=requested_by,
                            grounding=grounding,
                            run=run,
                        ),
                        timeout=budget,
                    )
            except LLMRateLimited as exc:
                retry_ms = max(0, int(exc.retry_after_s * 1000))
                await self._nak_step_rate_limited(
                    msg=msg,
                    org_id=org_id,
                    run_id=actual_run_id,
                    job_id=job_id,
                    step=step_id,
                    step_index=idx,
                    retry_ms=retry_ms,
                )
                return
            except Exception as exc:
                error_code, error_message = _classify_step_failure(exc, step_id=step_id, log=log)
                await self._fail_run(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    run_id=actual_run_id,
                    job_id=job_id,
                    step=step_id,
                    step_index=idx,
                    error_code=error_code,
                    error_message=error_message,
                )
                await msg.ack()
                return

            if step_id != _STEP_FINALIZE_SCENARIO:
                await self._emit_step_frame(
                    job_id=job_id,
                    org_id=org_id,
                    status="in_progress",
                    generated=idx + 1,
                    step=step_id,
                    step_index=idx,
                    step_status="done",
                )
            # else: _step_finalize_scenario already settled the run + the
            # job + emitted its own terminal "ready" frame.

        await msg.ack()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- rate limit

    async def _consume_rate_token(self, org_id: str) -> None:
        """Consume one token from this generator's dedicated rate-limit
        bucket; raises the SAME ``LLMRateLimited`` the gateway's own 429 path
        raises when the bucket is exhausted."""
        ok, retry_ms = await self.rate_limiter.consume(
            bucket_key=_bucket_key(org_id), org_id=org_id
        )
        if not ok:
            raise LLMRateLimited(retry_after_s=retry_ms / 1000.0)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- steps

    async def _step_fetch_odin(
        self, *, org_id: str, run_id: str, odin_template_id: str, seed: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> OdinGrounding:
        """Step 1: derive grounding from the ODIN cache (Task 6). No LLM
        call, no rate limiting."""
        loaded = await load_odin_oe_for_grounding(self.pool, odin_template_id=odin_template_id)
        if loaded is None:
            raise _OdinUnavailable(f"no cached ODIN template for id {odin_template_id!r}")
        oe, articles = loaded
        grounding = resolve_odin_grounding(
            oe,
            articles,
            objective_text=str(seed.get("objective_text") or ""),
            objective_category=str(seed.get("objective_category") or ""),
        )
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await q.odin_generation_run_set_step_done(
                conn,
                run_id=run_id,
                step=_STEP_FETCH_ODIN,
                steps_done=_STEP_INDEX[_STEP_FETCH_ODIN] + 1,
                grounding=_grounding_to_jsonb(grounding),
            )

    async def _step_generate_factions(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        run_id: str,
        job_id: str,
        requested_by: str,
        faction_draft_id: str,
        grounding: OdinGrounding,

        """Step 2: faction discovery, grounded in ODIN content.

        manual request today.

        objective_str = render_objective(grounding.objective.as_dict())
        description_str = grounding.description

        lock_key = f"faction_discovery:{org_id}:{faction_draft_id}"
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))", lock_key)
            discovery = await q.faction_discovery_upsert_pending(
                conn,
                org_id=org_id,
                discovery_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                requested_by=requested_by,
                job_id=job_id,
                draft_id=faction_draft_id,

        # Defensive empty-context guard (see _InsufficientOdinContent) —
        # should be unreachable given resolve_odin_grounding's non-empty-
        # description guarantee, kept for defense-in-depth against that
        # guarantee ever loosening.
        if not location_str.strip() and not objective_str.strip() and not description_str.strip():
            raise _InsufficientOdinContent(
                "ODIN grounding produced no location, objective, or description"
            )

        await self._consume_rate_token(org_id)

        count = faction_count if faction_count > 0 else _DEFAULT_COUNT
        candidates, confidence = await run_faction_discovery(
            llm=self.llm,
            location=location_str,
            objective=objective_str,

        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await q.faction_discovery_set_ready(
                conn,

                conn,
                run_id=run_id,

            "derived_fields": sorted(grounding.derived_fields),
        }

            await q.odin_generation_run_set_ready(conn, run_id=run_id, scenario=scenario)
            await emit_audit(

    async def _fail_run(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        run_id: str,
        job_id: str,
        step: str,
        step_index: int,
        error_code: str,
        error_message: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Flip the WHOLE RUN to a terminal error, settle the job, then frame."""
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await q.odin_generation_run_set_error(
                conn, run_id=run_id, step=step, error_code=error_code, error_message=error_message
            )
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await q.generation_job_settle(conn, job_id=job_id, status="error")
        await self._emit_step_frame(
            job_id=job_id,
            org_id=org_id,
            status="error",
            generated=step_index,
            step=step,
            step_index=step_index,
            step_status="failed",
            error=error_message,
            # The machine-readable twin of ``error``. The FE keys its
            # localized per-code copy off this; ``error_message`` is
            # server-generated English and cannot be translated.
            error_code=error_code,
        )

    async def _cancel(self, *, org_id: str, run_id: str, job_id: str, generated: int) -> None:
        """Settle the run + the job's own terminal status after a cancel
        checkpoint fires. No audit twin, no fan-out — a cancelled run is not
        a completed generation (mirrors FactionDiscoveryConsumer's own
        ``_cancel``)."""
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await _settle_cancelled(conn, run_id=run_id)
            await q.generation_job_set_status(conn, job_id=job_id, status="cancelled")
        await self._emit_step_frame(
            job_id=job_id, org_id=org_id, status="cancelled", generated=generated
        )

    async def _nak_step_rate_limited(
        self,
        *,
        msg: Any,
        org_id: str,
        run_id: str,
        job_id: str,
        step: str,
        step_index: int,
        retry_ms: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Rate-limit exhaustion (either OUR OWN token bucket or a raw
        ``LLMRateLimited`` from the LLM client): reset ``computing ->
        pending`` (preserving which step it was on), mark the step
        ``pending``, then NAK with the server-advised delay — but only
        AFTER a frame carrying ``retry_after_ms`` ships, so a long backoff
        is not unexplained silence on the wire."""
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            await _reset_run_to_pending(conn, run_id=run_id)
        await self._publish_rate_limited_frame(
            job_id=job_id, org_id=org_id, step=step, step_index=step_index, retry_after_ms=retry_ms
        )
        await msg.nak(delay=retry_ms / 1000.0)

    async def _emit_step_frame(
        self,
        *,
        job_id: str,
        org_id: str,
        status: str,
        generated: int,
        step: str | None = None,
        step_index: int | None = None,
        step_status: str | None = None,
        error: str | None = None,
        error_code: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        await emit_progress(
            self.publisher,
            job_id=job_id,
            status=status,
            generated=generated,
            total=_TOTAL_STEPS,
            error=error,
            org_id=org_id,
            step=step,
            step_index=step_index,
            step_status=step_status,
            error_code=error_code,
        )

    async def _publish_rate_limited_frame(
        self, *, job_id: str, org_id: str, step: str, step_index: int, retry_after_ms: int
    ) -> None:
        """A rate-limit-retry tick carrying ``retry_after_ms``.

        ``emit_progress``'s signature extension (Task 7) is scoped to
        ``step``/``step_index``/``step_status`` only, so this one extra,
        NAK-specific field is layered on with a direct
        ``publisher.publish`` call (the same underlying mechanism
        ``emit_progress`` itself uses) rather than growing that shared
        helper's signature further for a single caller.
        """
        body = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "status": "in_progress",
            "generated": step_index,
            "total": _TOTAL_STEPS,
            "step": step,
            "step_index": step_index,
            "step_status": "pending",
            "retry_after_ms": retry_after_ms,
        }
        try:
            await self.publisher.publish(
                f"range.job.progress.{job_id}", json.dumps(body).encode(), org_id=org_id
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # progress is best-effort
            _log.debug("rate-limit progress publish failed", err=str(exc))

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- poison

    async def _on_poison(self, msg: Any) -> None:
        """Last-chance hook on the FINAL delivery (num_delivered >=
        max_deliver). A run that never once got a rate-limit token across
        every redelivery attempt is the most plausible way to reach this —
        hence ``error_code='rate_limited'`` (the one persisted vocabulary
        value never otherwise written by ``_fail_run``, since a rate-limit
        hit is normally a NAK-retry, not terminal)."""
        try:
            payload = json.loads(msg.data)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return

        faction_draft_id = str(payload.get("faction_discovery_draft_id") or "")
        job_id = str(payload.get("job_id") or "")
        if not faction_draft_id or not job_id:
            return

        async with self.pool.with_drain() as conn:
            run = await q.odin_generation_run_get_by_draft(
                conn, faction_discovery_draft_id=faction_draft_id
            )
        if run is None or run.job_id != job_id:
            return

        step = run.step or _STEP_ORDER[0]
        await self._fail_run(
            org_id=run.org_id,
            run_id=run.id,
            job_id=job_id,
            step=step,
            step_index=_STEP_INDEX.get(step, 0),
            error_code="rate_limited",
            error_message="odin exercise generation failed after maximum retries — rate limited",
        )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- deadline sweep


async def sweep_expired_odin_generation_runs(pool: Any, publisher: Any) -> int:
    """One sweep tick: flip stuck runs (:func:`range_svc.repo.queries.
    odin_generation_sweep_expired`), settle each paired job row, and publish
    each terminal frame. Returns the count flipped."""
    swept = await q.odin_generation_sweep_expired(pool)
    for run in swept:
        if not run.job_id:
            continue
        async with pool.with_org(run.org_id) as conn:
            await q.generation_job_settle(conn, job_id=run.job_id, status="error")
        await emit_progress(
            publisher,
            job_id=run.job_id,
            status="error",
            generated=0,
            total=_TOTAL_STEPS,
            error="generation run exceeded its deadline and was stopped",
            org_id=run.org_id,
            step=run.step,
            step_status="failed",
            # Matches the ``error_code='timeout'`` the sweep writes to the
            # row, so a browser watching the live stream renders the same
            # localized timeout copy the poll fallback would show it.
            error_code="timeout",
        )
    return len(swept)


async def odin_generation_deadline_sweep_loop(
    pool: Any, publisher: Any, *, interval_s: float = ORPHAN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S
) -> None:
    """Periodic deadline sweep — runs until the task is cancelled (Task 7).
    Registered on the SAME hourly cadence as the other periodic sweeps in
    ``worker.py``."""
    while True:
        try:
            await sweep_expired_odin_generation_runs(pool, publisher)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            _log.warning("odin generation deadline sweep failed", err=str(exc))
        await asyncio.sleep(interval_s)

"""ODIN-cache grounding derivation for the ODIN-driven exercise generator
(ticket #1724 / T6).

The ODIN reference cache (``range.odin_operational_environment`` /
``range.odin_article``) stores NO article body text — only titles, PMESII
section labels, the five extracted infobox facts, a combatant-command
region band, tags, and a ``toc`` outline (see
``range_svc.odin.normalize``). This module turns that thin material into
the ``location``/``objective``/``temporal_context``/``description`` seed
fields an exercise draft needs, plus one sanitized, marker-wrapped
``reference_material`` block for the LLM prompt. This is the first place
ODIN cache text passes through ``omnicore_prompt_safety`` — every prior
consumer of this cache (the preview drawer) only ever rendered it to a UI,
never embedded it in a prompt.

Two hazards this module exists specifically to avoid:

1. **Silent truncation.** A single ``wrap_untrusted``/``sanitize_text``
   call caps at ``_MAX_SCALAR_LEN`` (4096) with no line awareness, which
   would decapitate a large reference block mid-content.
   :func:`omnicore_prompt_safety.structured_material_block` is used
   instead: each line is sanitized individually and the block is cut on
   whole-line boundaries only, from the end, once ``ODIN_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS``
   is exceeded — so as long as ``lines`` is built highest-priority-first
   (see :func:`_build_reference_lines`), truncation drops the least
   important content first.
2. **JSONB-repr leak.** ``infobox``/``toc`` are lists of
   ``{key, value, hasBorder, nested}`` / ``{name, children}`` dicts. This
   module never renders one via ``str(some_dict)`` — every line is built
   field-by-field from the five facts :func:`range_svc.odin.normalize.
   extract_infobox_facts` already extracts (never raw infobox rows), and
   the ``toc`` is only ever walked structurally via
   :func:`range_svc.odin.normalize.cap_toc_depth` and rendered by its
   ``name`` field.

Every read of the ODIN cache tables MUST go through the APP ROLE
(``pool.app.acquire()``) — see :func:`load_odin_oe_for_grounding`. Never
``pool.with_drain()``: the drainer role (``range_drainer``, BYPASSRLS) has

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Final

from omnicore_prompt_safety import structured_material_block

from range_svc.db.pool import Pool
from range_svc.odin.normalize import (
    InfoboxFacts,
    cap_toc_depth,
    extract_infobox_facts,
    group_articles_by_section,
)
from range_svc.repo.queries.odin_template import (
    OdinArticleRow,
    OdinOeDetailRow,
    odin_article_list_for_oe,

#: Total character budget for the assembled, marker-wrapped reference
#: block (#1724). Deliberately larger than ``omnicore_prompt_safety``'s
#: scalar ``_MAX_SCALAR_LEN`` (4096) default — a single-shot
#: ``wrap_untrusted`` at that cap silently decapitated ODIN grounding
#: content; :func:`_build_reference_block` routes through
#: ``structured_material_block`` instead, which truncates on whole-line
#: boundaries at THIS budget.
ODIN_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS: Final[int] = 6000

#: Per-PMESII-section article title cap, mirroring
#: ``range_svc.workers.generation.context_retrieval.ContextRetriever.
#: _DEFAULT_LIMIT`` (confirmed = 8 at the time this module was written) so
#: the ODIN grounding block and the RAG context-retrieval block agree on
#: how many items per group is "enough" for LLM grounding.
ODIN_ARTICLES_PER_SECTION_LIMIT: Final[int] = 8

#: Label prefixed to the marker-wrapped reference block, in the same style
#: as ``omnicore_prompt_safety.reference_material_block``/
#: ``source_material_block``'s own fixed labels.
ODIN_REFERENCE_LABEL: Final[str] = "Reference material from the ODIN operational-environment cache:"

#: Key recorded in :attr:`OdinGrounding.derived_fields` when ``objective``
#: was NOT client-supplied and was instead mechanically derived from the
#: OE's country name — lets a caller/UI badge it as such.
DERIVED_FIELD_OBJECTIVE: Final[str] = "objective"

#: Fixed category assigned to a derived (never client-supplied) objective.
_DERIVED_OBJECTIVE_CATEGORY: Final[str] = "information_operations"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OdinLocation:
    """The exercise-draft ``location`` fields derived from one cached OE.

    ``region`` is ALWAYS ``""`` — ODIN's own ``region`` column is a
    COMBATANT-COMMAND band (``africa|eurasia|europe|indo_pacific|polar``),
    not a sub-national region, and must never leak into this field. The
    band is still surfaced, but only as labelled provenance text inside
    :attr:`OdinGrounding.reference_material` (see
    :func:`_build_reference_lines`).
    """

    country: str
    town: str
    region: str

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """``{country, town, region}`` projection — consumers key off these
        field names, never dict iteration order, so this insertion order is
        not load-bearing at any call site."""
        return {"country": self.country, "town": self.town, "region": self.region}


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OdinObjective:
    """The exercise-draft ``objective`` fields — either client-supplied
    (via ``objective_text``/``objective_category`` in
    :func:`resolve_odin_grounding`) or mechanically derived."""

    text: str
    category: str

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """``{text, category}`` projection."""
        return {"text": self.text, "category": self.category}


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OdinGrounding:
    """Everything :func:`resolve_odin_grounding` derives from one cached
    OE (plus its articles and an optional client seed): the four
    exercise-draft scenario fields, the sanitized reference block, and
    provenance for any field that was mechanically derived rather than
    client-supplied.

    ``description`` is NEVER empty (see :func:`_derive_description`) —
    the discovery consumer's empty-context guard
    (``faction_discovery/consumer.py``'s Step 4b) hard-fails only when
    location, objective, AND description are ALL blank, and an empty
    ``description`` here would trip it for the ~20/53 OEs with no infobox
    and no articles.
    """

    location: OdinLocation
    objective: OdinObjective
    temporal_context: str
    description: str
    reference_material: str
    derived_fields: frozenset[str]


def _derive_objective(country: str) -> OdinObjective:
    return OdinObjective(
        text=f"Understand and shape the information environment in {country}.",
        category=_DERIVED_OBJECTIVE_CATEGORY,
    )


def _resolve_objective(
    country: str, *, objective_text: str, objective_category: str
) -> tuple[OdinObjective, frozenset[str]]:
    """``objective`` <- the caller-supplied seed when ``objective_text`` is
    non-blank, else the mechanical fallback (recorded in
    ``derived_fields``)."""
    if objective_text.strip():
        return OdinObjective(text=objective_text, category=objective_category), frozenset()
    return _derive_objective(country), frozenset({DERIVED_FIELD_OBJECTIVE})


def _resolve_temporal_context(temporal_dates: Sequence[str]) -> str:
    """``temporal_context`` <- the seed's dates, joined, when supplied; else
    ``""``. Never fabricates a date when the seed carries none."""
    dates = [d.strip() for d in temporal_dates if d and d.strip()]
    return ", ".join(dates)


def _derive_description(title: str, facts: InfoboxFacts) -> str:
    """A mechanical, present-facts-only clause render of ``title`` + the
    five infobox facts — only the government/population/languages/ethnic
    clauses whose fact is actually present are emitted; a NULL fact's
    clause is skipped entirely rather than rendered as ``"Government:
    None."``. Degrades to ``f"{title} operational environment."`` alone
    when every fact is absent — this is what keeps the result non-empty
    for the ~20/53 OEs with no infobox and no articles."""
    clauses: list[str] = [f"{title} operational environment."]
    if facts.government:
        clauses.append(f"Government: {facts.government}.")
    if facts.population:
        clauses.append(f"Population: {facts.population}.")
    if facts.official_languages:
        clauses.append(f"Official languages: {', '.join(facts.official_languages)}.")
    if facts.ethnic_groups:
        clauses.append(f"Major ethnic groups: {', '.join(facts.ethnic_groups)}.")
    return " ".join(clauses)


def _identity_and_facts_lines(oe: OdinOeDetailRow, facts: InfoboxFacts) -> list[str]:
    """Priority-1 lines: identity + the five extracted infobox facts.
    NEVER dropped by the caller's truncation ordering — this is always the
    first section fed to ``structured_material_block``. Rendered strictly
    field-by-field from :class:`InfoboxFacts` (never a raw infobox row) so
    layout flags (``hasBorder``/``nested``) and self-referential garbage
    never reach the prompt."""
    lines = [f"Operational Environment: {oe.title}"]
    if oe.infobox_official_name:
        lines.append(f"Official Name: {oe.infobox_official_name}")
    if facts.capital:
        lines.append(f"Capital: {facts.capital}")
    if facts.government:
        lines.append(f"Government: {facts.government}")
    if facts.population:
        lines.append(f"Population: {facts.population}")
    if facts.official_languages:
        lines.append(f"Official Languages: {', '.join(facts.official_languages)}")
    if facts.ethnic_groups:
        lines.append(f"Ethnic Groups: {', '.join(facts.ethnic_groups)}")
    return lines


def _band_and_tags_lines(oe: OdinOeDetailRow) -> list[str]:
    """Priority-2 lines: the combatant-command band and tags, explicitly
    labelled as ODIN provenance so the model (and any future reader of the
    raw prompt) cannot mistake the band for a sub-national region."""
    lines = [
        f"Combatant Command Band: {oe.region} (ODIN classification, not a sub-national region)"
    ]
    if oe.tags:
        lines.append(f"Tags: {', '.join(oe.tags)}")
    return lines


def _pmesii_article_lines(articles: Sequence[OdinArticleRow]) -> list[str]:
    """Priority-3 lines: article titles grouped by PMESII-PT section,
    capped at :data:`ODIN_ARTICLES_PER_SECTION_LIMIT` per section. Empty
    sections are omitted entirely — unlike the preview drawer's skeleton
    (which needs all 8 for a UI heading), a prompt gains nothing from a
    header with no titles under it."""
    lines: list[str] = []
    for group in group_articles_by_section(articles):
        if not group.articles:
            continue
        label = group.section or "Unspecified"
        lines.append(f"PMESII Section — {label}:")
        lines.extend(f"  - {a.title}" for a in group.articles[:ODIN_ARTICLES_PER_SECTION_LIMIT])
    return lines


def _flatten_toc(node: Mapping[str, Any], *, depth: int, out: list[str]) -> None:
    name = node.get("name")
    out.append(f"{'  ' * (depth - 1)}- {name if isinstance(name, str) else ''}")
    children = node.get("children")
    if isinstance(children, list):
        for child in children:
            if isinstance(child, Mapping):
                _flatten_toc(child, depth=depth + 1, out=out)


def _toc_outline_lines(toc: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[str]:
    """Priority-4 (lowest) lines: the ``toc`` outline, depth-capped via
    :func:`range_svc.odin.normalize.cap_toc_depth` and flattened to one
    indented line per node. This is the first section dropped (in whole
    trailing lines) once the assembled block exceeds
    :data:`ODIN_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS`."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for node in toc:
        if isinstance(node, Mapping):
            _flatten_toc(cap_toc_depth(node), depth=1, out=out)
    if not out:
        return []
    return ["Article Outline (Table of Contents):", *out]


def _build_reference_lines(
    oe: OdinOeDetailRow, facts: InfoboxFacts, articles: Sequence[OdinArticleRow]
) -> list[str]:
    """Assemble every candidate line, STRICTLY in priority order (1 =
    identity/facts, highest, through 4 = toc outline, lowest). Passed
    as-is to ``structured_material_block``, whose own truncation drops
    whole trailing lines once ``max_len`` is exceeded — priority ordering
    here is what makes that truncation drop the least valuable content
    first rather than mid-way through the identity facts."""
    return [
        *_identity_and_facts_lines(oe, facts),
        *_band_and_tags_lines(oe),
        *_pmesii_article_lines(articles),
        *_toc_outline_lines(oe.toc),
    ]


def _build_reference_block(
    oe: OdinOeDetailRow, facts: InfoboxFacts, articles: Sequence[OdinArticleRow]
) -> str:
    lines = _build_reference_lines(oe, facts, articles)
    return structured_material_block(ODIN_REFERENCE_LABEL, lines, max_len=ODIN_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS)


def resolve_odin_grounding(
    oe: OdinOeDetailRow,
    articles: Sequence[OdinArticleRow],
    *,
    objective_text: str = "",
    objective_category: str = "",
    temporal_dates: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> OdinGrounding:
    """Pure derivation: one cached OE + its articles (already fetched via
    :func:`load_odin_oe_for_grounding`) + an optional client-supplied seed
    -> the full :class:`OdinGrounding`.

    ``objective_text``/``objective_category``/``temporal_dates`` are the
    request's seed values, already unpacked by the caller from whatever
    wire type it holds (e.g. a future ``OdinScenarioSeed`` proto) — this
    function takes no dependency on that type. ``objective_text`` blank
    (the default) means "no seed objective supplied", never a real empty
    value a caller wants persisted; ``objective`` is then mechanically
    derived and :data:`DERIVED_FIELD_OBJECTIVE` is recorded in
    ``derived_fields``. There is no seed override for ``location`` or
    ``description`` — see the module docstring's derivation rules.

    Never raises: an OE with no infobox and no articles (~20/53) still
    produces every field, with ``description`` degrading to
    ``f"{oe.title} operational environment."`` alone.
    """
    facts = extract_infobox_facts(oe.infobox)
    country = oe.infobox_official_name or oe.title
    location = OdinLocation(country=country, town=facts.capital or "", region="")
    objective, derived_fields = _resolve_objective(
        country, objective_text=objective_text, objective_category=objective_category
    )
    return OdinGrounding(
        location=location,
        objective=objective,
        temporal_context=_resolve_temporal_context(temporal_dates),
        description=_derive_description(oe.title, facts),
        reference_material=_build_reference_block(oe, facts, articles),
        derived_fields=derived_fields,
    )


async def load_odin_oe_for_grounding(
    pool: Pool, *, odin_template_id: str
) -> tuple[OdinOeDetailRow, list[OdinArticleRow]] | None:
    """Fetch one OE + its articles from the ODIN cache for grounding.

    Reads on the APP ROLE ONLY (``pool.app.acquire()``) — never
    ``pool.with_drain()``: ``range_drainer`` (BYPASSRLS) has no grants on
    ``range.odin_operational_environment``/``range.odin_article`` at all,
    and there is no ``pool.with_org()`` GUC to set either, since these
    tables carry no ``org_id``/RLS (platform-global cache — see
    ``repo/queries/odin_template.py``'s module docstring). Mirrors
    ``handlers/odin_template.py``'s ``List``/``Get``, which use the
    identical ``self.repo.pool.app.acquire()`` + one transaction pattern
    for a consistent snapshot across the two reads.

    Returns ``None`` when ``odin_template_id`` has no cached row (mirrors
    ``odin_oe_get``'s own ``None`` contract) — the caller decides how to
    surface that (e.g. ``error_code='odin_unavailable'``).
    """
    async with pool.app.acquire() as conn, conn.transaction():
        oe = await odin_oe_get(conn, identifier=odin_template_id)
        if oe is None:
            return None
        articles = await odin_article_list_for_oe(conn, oe_identifier=odin_template_id)
    return oe, articles
